name: Getting models to follow detailed instructions better
gist: These papers improve how well models follow specific instructions and learn from feedback using preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and fine-tuning techniques.
explain: Imagine you ask a model to write a poem in a specific style, with specific constraints, and the model mostly ignores your constraints and does its own thing. This happens because models trained on internet text learn many different writing styles but have not learned to rank your particular instructions as more important than their default patterns. Papers in this area focus on making models respect and follow detailed instructions precisely. The core idea is fine-tuning: after a model learns basic language patterns, you show it many examples of what good instruction-following looks like and train it to match that behavior.

One effective technique is preference optimization, where instead of just showing the model correct outputs, you show it pairs of outputs—one good and one bad—and train the model to prefer the good one. This works because the model already understands language well, so it just needs to learn to steer toward human preferences. Another approach uses reinforcement learning with a reward signal that scores how well the model followed the instructions. The model learns which behaviors get rewarded and leans into them. The challenge is that feedback has to be consistent and signal real information, so creating good training signals becomes a central problem.

The result is models that actually do what you ask instead of doing something similar-ish. This matters for practical applications because users become frustrated when models do not listen, and it matters for safety because a model that does not follow instructions is unpredictable. Papers show that careful fine-tuning can make a model follow instructions much more reliably, and this skill does not require training on trillions more examples—just thousands of well-chosen examples with clear feedback.

papers.contribution: On temporal information retrieval, TPOUR Contriever improves average nDCG@5 by +4.04 (+12.15%) on explicit and +4.98 (+15.21%) on implicit queries while being 72.7× smaller than Qwen-Embedding-8B.

papers.title: Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future
papers.contribution: Across Llama, Qwen, and Mistral model families, reaches 29.44 win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 for Llama3.1-8B, outperforming self-rewarding baseline (19.69) by 9.75, with superior out-of-distribution generalization.

papers.title: The Differences Between Direct Alignment Algorithms are a Blur
papers.contribution: Reveals that the ranking objective is the primary determinant of alignment quality, while the specific scalar score is secondary.

papers.title: The Geometry of Updates: Fisher Alignment at Vocabulary Scale
papers.contribution: FisherSketch makes K=128,256 head Fisher alignment practical with 16 KB task signatures and 192 KB per-task streaming state, providing diagnostic instruments for studying whether LLM task similarity is driven by activations, errors, or coupling.

papers.title: Think Fast and Slow: Step-Level Cognitive Depth Adaptation for LLM Agents
papers.contribution: CogRouter achieves state-of-the-art performance on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld with superior efficiency through step-level cognitive adaptation.

papers.title: TiME: Test-Time Mixture-of-Experts Routing via Asymmetric CO-Optimal Transport for Continual Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines in continual test-time adaptation by correctly routing shifting domains and maintaining the adaptability-stability balance.

papers.title: ToMAP: Training Opponent-Aware LLM Persuaders with Theory of Mind
papers.contribution: A 3B ToMAP persuader outperforms much larger baselines like GPT-4o with relative gain of 39.4%; exhibits complex reasoning and reduced repetition leading to more diverse arguments.

papers.title: Token-Importance Guided Direct Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves higher accuracy and stronger generative diversity with more stable and computationally efficient solutions compared to DPO.

papers.title: TokenRatio: Principled Token-Level Preference Optimization via Ratio Matching
papers.contribution: Improves alignment quality and training stability while increasing output diversity relative to sequence-level and token-level baselines.

papers.title: Toward Effective Tool-Integrated Reasoning via Self-Evolved Preference Learning
papers.contribution: Tests on 10 datasets show Tool-Light significantly improves efficiency and accuracy of tool-integrated reasoning across models.

papers.title: Toward Robust Multilingual Adaptation of LLMs for Low-Resource Languages
papers.contribution: Shows bounded representation deviation and stable downstream behavior; consistently improves multilingual baselines on retrieval, ranking, QA, and reasoning with five Southeast Asian and two South Asian languages.

papers.title: Towards Multimodal Large Language Models with Both Training and Inference Efficiency
papers.contribution: SAISA achieves superior performance with significantly reduced computational costs across various baseline models, sizes, and training datasets.

papers.title: Towards On-Policy SFT: Distribution Discriminant Theory and its Applications in LLM Training
papers.contribution: On-Policy SFT achieves generalization performance on par with prominent offline RL algorithms while maintaining SFT efficiency.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Valuable Preference Data for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.contribution: The method enables more precise selection of valuable preference data, with models achieving better alignment across diverse benchmarks and LLM families through model-specific data selection.

papers.title: Training Large Language Models To Reason In Parallel With Global Forking Tokens
papers.contribution: Set Supervised Fine-Tuning preserves unique reasoning modes and produces emergent global forking tokens, outperforming standard fine-tuning on reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Turning Internal Gap into Self-Improvement: Promoting the Generation-Understanding Unification in MLLMs
papers.contribution: Self-improvement significantly enhances generation and promotes MLLM unification; co-improvement effect during post-training drives aligned learning dynamics between generation and understanding.

papers.title: What Generative Search Engines Like and How to Optimize Web Content Cooperatively
papers.contribution: Framework demonstrates effectiveness in enhancing content traction while preserving search utility with learned rules robust to domain variants.

papers.title: When Simple Problems Wear Complex Costumes: Improving Efficiency in LRM's Adaptive Reasoning
papers.contribution: The model reduces computational overhead while preserving accuracy and demonstrates improved robustness to misleading linguistic cues.

papers.title: When Tabular Foundation Models Meet Strategic Tabular Data: A Prior Alignment Approach
papers.contribution: SPN consistently improves robustness and predictive performance under strategic manipulation on real-world and synthetic datasets without retraining foundation models.

papers.title: Why DPO is a Misspecified Estimator and How to Fix It
papers.contribution: AuxDPO mitigates misspecification in DPO with superior performance on bandit settings and LLM alignment tasks compared to vanilla DPO.

papers.title: ssToken: Self-modulated and Semantic-aware Token Selection for LLM Fine-tuning
papers.contribution: Both self-modulated and semantic-aware selection outperform full-data fine-tuning, with integration delivering synergistic gains exceeding prior token-level methods.
